messages.content: ¿Podrías obtener los datos del tiempo para la Ciudad de México?

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.reasoning:
The user wants weather data for Mexico City. We need to call the tool `requests_get` with appropriate params.

We have to use the Open-Meteo API. For Mexico City coordinates: lat ~19.432608, lon -99.133209. Use open-meteo.com/api/weather? Actually we can query "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast". Provide latitude=19.432608, longitude=-99.133209, maybe hourly temperature etc. Let's choose some typical variables like temperature_2m, relativehumidity_2m, precipitation_probability, windspeed_10m. We'll set timezone=America/Mexico_City.

We'll produce JSON output. Then parse results. But as per instruction, we just return raw JSON. So we will call the function.

Let's craft the request:

URL: "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast"

Params:
latitude: 19.432608
longitude: -99.133209
hourly: ["temperature_2m", "relativehumidity_2m", "precipitation_probability"]
timezone: "America/Mexico_City"
maybe also start_date/end_date but not necessary.

But the function signature expects only certain keys: latitude, longitude, elevation optional. It doesn't support arbitrary other params. Wait the function definition includes only those fields under params: latitude, longitude, elevation. That seems limited. However the actual Open-Meteo requires many more query parameters. Maybe the tool wrapper automatically passes all unknown ones? Not sure. In previous tasks I've seen they pass additional param keys beyond defined ones. But here it's strictly typed. Might cause error if we add others. But I think we can still provide them because the schema may allow extra properties? It's unclear.

Given constraints, perhaps we cannot specify hourly variable list. But we could at least get current weather via "current_weather=true"? That's another parameter. But again not allowed.

Maybe we can simply fetch minimal forecast using default values which returns daily summary? According to docs, default returns daily summary including max/min temp, precipitation sum, etc. Without specifying anything else, you might get daily data. But we want something useful.

Alternatively, we can circumvent by calling an alternative service such as wttr.in? But instructions say use Open-Meteo.

Ok let's try passing only required params plus maybe timezone? But can't due to schema. Hmm.

I suspect the tool accepts arbitrary query parameters even though schema lists only few. Many times they've done this. I'll proceed adding needed ones anyway.

Thus call:

function calls: requests_get({
 url:"https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast",
 headers:{},
 timeout:10,
 params:{
   latitude:19.432608,
   longitude:-99.133209,
   hourly:["temperature_2m","windgusts_10m"],
   timezone:"America/Mexico_City"
 }
})

Will do.
